layer.name: Testing Layer
layer.description: Describes how the system is verified: test strategies and plans, suites and cases, fixtures and test data, mocks and stubs, coverage targets and summaries, and the environments tests run in (IEEE 829-2008 test documentation). Test files, fixtures and test configuration are evidence for elements here; the production code under test belongs to the layer it implements.

contextvariation.title: ContextVariation
contextvariation.description: A named test-design condition, classified by test type (functional, load, security, regression, smoke, exploratory), under which a TestCoverageTarget is to be exercised, optionally bound to a set of EnvironmentFactors that fix the concrete environment for that condition. It names the whole execution context. It does not name a single environmental variable or an input value. Use EnvironmentFactor instead when the element is a single concrete environmental variable and its value (e.g. 'Ubuntu 22.04', 'en-US', 'latency < 100ms'), not a named test context that groups such variables. Use CoverageRequirement instead when the element states coverage criteria (pairwise, boundary-values, MC/DC) that must be met, possibly across several contexts, rather than defining one context. Use InputSpacePartition instead when the variation is in the data fed to the target (an input field's equivalence classes), not in the type of test or the execution environment. Use OutcomeCategory instead when the element classifies the expected result (success, timeout, validation-error), not the conditions under which the test runs.

description.description: Free-text explanation of the execution condition this variation represents: its purpose, scope and how it differs from other contexts applied to the same target, such as 'peak-load run at 500 rps against staging'. Set it whenever the contextType alone does not identify the context uniquely.

contextType.description: The category of test context this variation represents

environmentFactors.description: References EnvironmentFactor nodes specifying the concrete environmental constraints (OS, locale, network, hardware, dependency versions) that define this context variation.

contextvariation.x-dr-standard: IEEE 829-2008 Test Design Specification – Approach refinements and Environmental needs (Clause 9 Level Test Plan: environmental needs)
x-dr-evidence: Separate test suites or directories split by test type, such as tests/load, tests/security, tests/smoke, or pytest markers / JUnit @Tag('smoke'|'regression') used to select runs
CI pipeline jobs or matrix entries that run the same targets under named contexts, e.g. a 'load' job invoking k6/JMeter or a 'security' job invoking OWASP ZAP, each with its own environment variables

Test configuration profiles bundling environment settings per context, e.g. playwright.config projects, tox envs, or application-test-load.yml, that set OS, locale, network throttling or dependency versions

x-dr-distinguish.testing.coveragerequirement: the element states coverage criteria (pairwise, boundary-values, MC/DC) that must be met, possibly across several contexts, rather than defining one context
x-dr-distinguish.testing.inputspacepartition: the variation is in the data fed to the target (an input field's equivalence classes), not in the type of test or the execution environment
x-dr-distinguish.testing.outcomecategory: the element classifies the expected result (success, timeout, validation-error), not the conditions under which the test runs

coverageexclusion.title: CoverageExclusion
coverageexclusion.description: A recorded governance decision that removes a specific coverage target or coverage requirement from the coverage that must be achieved. It names the excluded item, gives the rationale, states whether the residual risk is accepted, and identifies the accountable approver. It exists only once someone has explicitly decided and signed off on not testing the item, not merely when the item is observed to be untested. Use CoverageGap instead when the missing coverage has been detected (e.g. in a summary report) but no one has yet approved leaving it untested; a gap may later flow into an exclusion. Use InputPartitionSelection instead when specific partition values are carved out of a single requirement's selection as a test-design choice (excludeValues), without a formal waiver, approver or risk acceptance. Use CoverageRequirement instead when the element states coverage criteria that must be satisfied rather than a sanctioned decision not to satisfy them. Use TestCaseSketch instead when an individual designed test case is being retired (status deprecated) rather than an entire target or requirement being waived from coverage.

description.description: Free-text summary of what is excluded and the scope of the exclusion; set it when the reason alone does not make the boundary of the excluded item clear.

reason.description: Plain-language justification for excluding the item from coverage (e.g. 'third-party code', 'deprecated endpoint scheduled for removal', 'not testable in CI environment'); always required.

riskAccepted.description: True when the approver has explicitly accepted the residual risk of the item going untested. False when the exclusion rests on the item having no meaningful risk (e.g. dead or generated code).

approvedBy.description: Name, role or identity reference of the person or body accountable for authorising the exclusion (e.g. 'QA Lead', 'jane.doe', 'Change Advisory Board'); always required.

affectedTargetRef.description: ID of the testing.testcoveragetarget or testing.coveragerequirement being excluded from coverage

dateApproved.description: ISO date when the exclusion was formally approved, supporting audit trail requirements

coverageexclusion.x-dr-standard: IEEE 829-2008 Clause 9 Level Test Plan: features not to be tested (with risk justification under risks and contingencies)
x-dr-evidence: A coverage-tool ignore entry with a justification comment that cites an approval or ticket, such as a `# pragma: no cover` or `/* istanbul ignore next */` line, `omit` in .coveragerc, or `coveragePathIgnorePatterns` in jest.config.
A test-waiver or exclusions file (YAML, JSON or Markdown) listing excluded endpoints, workflows or requirements with fields such as reason, approver and date.

A skipped or disabled test annotation that carries a reason and a waiver reference, such as `@pytest.mark.skip(reason="waived per QA-123, approved by J. Doe")` or `@Disabled("Excluded: risk accepted, see ADR-12")`.

x-dr-distinguish.testing.coveragegap: the missing coverage has been detected (e.g. in a summary report) but no one has yet approved leaving it untested; a gap may later flow into an exclusion.
x-dr-distinguish.testing.inputpartitionselection: specific partition values are carved out of a single requirement's selection as a test-design choice (excludeValues), without a formal waiver, approver or risk acceptance.
x-dr-distinguish.testing.coveragerequirement: the element states coverage criteria that must be satisfied rather than a sanctioned decision not to satisfy them.
x-dr-distinguish.testing.testcasesketch: an individual designed test case is being retired (status deprecated) rather than an entire target or requirement being waived from coverage.

coveragegap.title: CoverageGap
coveragegap.description: A recorded finding that a specific coverage requirement or coverage target lacks the implemented or executed tests it needs. It names what is uncovered, how severe the gap is, and where it stands in remediation. It records a shortfall against required coverage, not a deliberate, approved scope decision and not an aggregate metric. Use CoverageExclusion instead when the uncovered item has been formally approved as out of scope, with a rationale, accepted risk and a named approver, rather than merely found to be missing coverage. Use TargetCoverageSummary instead when you are recording counts or percentages of sketches and implemented tests for a target, rather than a specific uncovered requirement that needs action. Use CoverageSummary instead when the artifact aggregates coverage totals across the whole model instead of describing one identified deficit. Use CoverageRequirement instead when you are specifying the criteria that must be met, rather than recording that those criteria are currently unmet.

description.description: Free-text explanation of what is not covered (for example, missing partitions, contexts or outcome categories) and how the gap was detected. Set it whenever the severity and affected requirement alone do not make the gap clear.

severity.description: Risk level of leaving this gap unaddressed

affectedRequirements.description: Identifier or reference to the requirement(s) that remain uncovered due to this gap.

remediationStatus.description: Lifecycle state of this coverage gap.

targetRef.description: ID of the testing.testcoveragetarget where this gap was identified

coveragegap.x-dr-standard: IEEE 829-2008 Clause 16 Level Test Report / Clause 17 Master Test Report (the Test Summary Report in IEEE 829-1998): comprehensive assessment and variances, i.e. identification of features or combinations not sufficiently tested
x-dr-evidence: Coverage tool output (e.g. lcov, JaCoCo, coverage.py) or a CI gate failure listing files or endpoints below a configured threshold such as `fail_under` or `coverageThreshold`.
Test files carrying skip or todo markers (`@pytest.mark.skip`, `it.todo`, `xit`, `@Disabled`) with a comment or ticket ID explaining that a requirement or partition is not yet tested.
Issue-tracker items or TEST_GAPS / test-report markdown entries labelled 'coverage gap' or 'missing tests', naming an endpoint or requirement ID and a severity.

x-dr-distinguish.testing.coverageexclusion: the uncovered item has been formally approved as out of scope, with a rationale, accepted risk and a named approver, rather than merely found to be missing coverage
x-dr-distinguish.testing.targetcoveragesummary: you are recording counts or percentages of sketches and implemented tests for a target, rather than a specific uncovered requirement that needs action
x-dr-distinguish.testing.coveragesummary: the artifact aggregates coverage totals across the whole model instead of describing one identified deficit
x-dr-distinguish.testing.coveragerequirement: you are specifying the criteria that must be met, rather than recording that those criteria are currently unmet

coveragerequirement.title: CoverageRequirement
coveragerequirement.description: A test design rule attached to one TestCoverageTarget that names a combinatorial or structural coverage criterion (e.g. boundary-values, pairwise, MC/DC) which the target's test cases must satisfy across selected input partitions, context variations and outcome categories. It states what must be exercised. It is not a test case, not the target itself, and not a measured result. Use TestCoverageTarget instead when the element identifies the endpoint, workflow, component or job that needs testing, rather than the criterion its tests must meet. Use InputPartitionSelection instead when the element lists which specific values of one InputSpacePartition are included or excluded, rather than the overall coverage strategy that uses those selections. Use TestCaseSketch instead when the element is one designed or implemented test case choosing concrete partition values, rather than the rule that a set of such cases must satisfy. Use CoverageGap instead when the element records a measured shortfall against a requirement found during reporting, rather than the requirement itself.

description.description: Free-text statement of what this requirement demands for its target, naming the partitions, contexts or outcomes in scope and any rationale. Set it whenever the coverageCriteria value alone does not make the scope evident.

coverageCriteria.description: The coverage strategy defining which combinations of partition values must be exercised

priority.description: Relative importance of fulfilling this coverage requirement

coveragerequirement.x-dr-standard: IEEE 829-2008 Clause 10 Level Test Design (test design specification: approach refinements and feature pass/fail criteria)
x-dr-evidence: A combinatorial test model file, such as a PICT .txt model, an allpairs config or a hypothesis/fast-check strategy, scoped to one endpoint or function, that declares parameters and an order or strategy like pairwise.

A parametrized test table (pytest.mark.parametrize, test.each, JUnit @ParameterizedTest/@CsvSource) whose rows enumerate boundary and invalid classes for one target, with a comment or docstring naming the criterion (e.g. 'boundary values for quantity').

A test plan or test design Markdown/YAML entry that states, per feature or endpoint, a required criterion and priority (e.g. 'POST /orders: all-partitions over status × role, must cover validation-error and authorization-error outcomes').

x-dr-distinguish.testing.testcoveragetarget: the element identifies the endpoint, workflow, component or job that needs testing, rather than the criterion its tests must meet
x-dr-distinguish.testing.inputpartitionselection: the element lists which specific values of one InputSpacePartition are included or excluded, rather than the overall coverage strategy that uses those selections
x-dr-distinguish.testing.testcasesketch: the element is one designed or implemented test case choosing concrete partition values, rather than the rule that a set of such cases must satisfy
x-dr-distinguish.testing.coveragegap: the element records a measured shortfall against a requirement found during reporting, rather than the requirement itself

coveragesummary.title: CoverageSummary
coveragesummary.description: A model-wide test summary report record that totals the coverage targets, coverage requirements and test case sketches of exactly one TestCoverageModel at a point in time. Per-target figures are rolled up from the model's TargetCoverageSummary records. Use TargetCoverageSummary instead when the metrics (sketch, implemented and automated counts or a percentage) describe a single TestCoverageTarget rather than the whole model. Use CoverageGap instead when the artifact records one specific shortfall between required and achieved coverage, with a severity and a remediation status, rather than aggregate totals. Use TestCoverageModel instead when the artifact is the coverage specification itself, holding the targets, partitions and requirements, rather than a generated report about it. Use CoverageExclusion instead when the artifact is an approved decision to leave a target or requirement uncovered, rather than a count of what is covered.

modelRef.description: ID of the testing.testcoveragemodel this summary aggregates

generatedAt.description: ISO 8601 date-time at which the summary was computed; set it every time the summary is regenerated so stale reports can be detected.

totalTargets.description: Non-negative count of TestCoverageTarget nodes in the referenced model at generation time, including targets that have exclusions or gaps.

totalRequirements.description: Non-negative count of CoverageRequirement nodes across all targets in the referenced model at generation time.

totalSketches.description: Non-negative count of TestCaseSketch nodes across all targets in the model regardless of status; this equals the sum of sketchCount over the model's TargetCoverageSummary records.

coveragesummary.x-dr-standard: IEEE 829-2008 Clause 17 Master Test Report / Clause 16 Level Test Report (overview and summary of results; the Test Summary Report in IEEE 829-1998)
x-dr-evidence: A script or CI job that loads the test coverage model (YAML or JSON) and emits totals of targets, requirements and test cases with a generation timestamp.
A generated report artifact (e.g. coverage-model-summary.json or a Markdown table in docs/testing) that lists overall counts per model and links to per-target summaries.
A test-reporting dashboard or README section that publishes model-level totals of covered features, requirements and designed test cases for a named application.

x-dr-distinguish.testing.targetcoveragesummary: the metrics (sketch, implemented and automated counts or a percentage) describe a single TestCoverageTarget rather than the whole model.
x-dr-distinguish.testing.coveragegap: the artifact records one specific shortfall between required and achieved coverage, with a severity and a remediation status, rather than aggregate totals.
x-dr-distinguish.testing.testcoveragemodel: the artifact is the coverage specification itself, holding the targets, partitions and requirements, rather than a generated report about it.
x-dr-distinguish.testing.coverageexclusion: the artifact is an approved decision to leave a target or requirement uncovered, rather than a count of what is covered.

environmentfactor.title: EnvironmentFactor
environmentfactor.description: A single named environmental condition of a test run (operating system, network characteristic, locale, hardware configuration or dependency version) pinned to a concrete value or constraint and recorded because it changes how tests behave. It describes one factor of the execution environment, not the test type that bundles factors together nor any input supplied to the system under test. Use ContextVariation instead when the thing being modelled is a named test context (functional, load, security, regression, smoke, exploratory) that groups several environmental constraints, rather than one variable with one value. Use PartitionValue instead when the value is an equivalence class of an input field passed to the system under test (request parameter, form field, data property), not a property of the runtime environment. Use InputSpacePartition instead when an input dimension is being divided into equivalence classes. Do this even if that dimension is a locale or OS selector. A single fixed environmental setting is not a partition.

factorType.description: Category of environmental variable being documented.

value.description: The specific value or constraint for this factor (e.g., 'Ubuntu 22.04', 'latency < 100ms', 'en-US', 'Node.js 20.x').

expectedRange.description: Acceptable range or set of values for this factor in the test environment (e.g., 'latency 50-200ms', 'Ubuntu 20.04 or 22.04').

testImpact.description: Description of how variations in this factor are expected to affect test behavior or outcomes.

description.description: Free-text explanation of what this environmental factor is and why it is pinned for testing, for example 'Server-side timezone forced to UTC to make date-boundary tests deterministic'. Set it whenever the factorType and value alone do not make the factor's purpose clear.

environmentfactor.x-dr-standard: IEEE 829-2008 Test Design Specification / Test Plan §'Environmental needs' (hardware, software, communications and tool characteristics of the test environment)
x-dr-evidence: A CI matrix entry pinning an environment axis, such as a GitHub Actions `strategy.matrix` with `os: [ubuntu-22.04, windows-2022]` or `node-version: [18.x, 20.x]`, or a tox/nox env list over Python versions.

Test setup that forces an environmental condition, such as setting `TZ`/`LANG`/`LC_ALL` environment variables, network-throttling or latency-injection config (toxiproxy, tc netem, Playwright `emulateNetworkConditions`), or a docker-compose test service pinned to a specific image tag.

Conditional test guards keyed on the environment, such as `@pytest.mark.skipif(sys.platform == 'win32')`, Jest `testEnvironment`, or an engines/`.nvmrc`/`.tool-versions` file referenced by test configuration.

x-dr-distinguish.testing.contextvariation: the thing being modelled is a named test context (functional, load, security, regression, smoke, exploratory) that groups several environmental constraints, rather than one variable with one value.
x-dr-distinguish.testing.partitionvalue: the value is an equivalence class of an input field passed to the system under test (request parameter, form field, data property), not a property of the runtime environment.
x-dr-distinguish.testing.inputspacepartition: an input dimension is being divided into equivalence classes. Do this even if that dimension is a locale or OS selector. A single fixed environmental setting is not a partition.

inputpartitionselection.title: InputPartitionSelection
inputpartitionselection.description: A coverage-scope rule within a CoverageRequirement that names exactly one InputSpacePartition and declares which of its PartitionValues must be exercised. The rule takes one of two forms: an explicit include list, or all values minus an exclude list. It selects equivalence classes and never binds concrete test data. Use InputSelection instead when a single partition value is bound to a concrete test datum for one specific TestCaseSketch, rather than a set of classes being declared in scope for a requirement. Use PartitionValue instead when you are defining the equivalence class itself (its label, constraint and representative value), not choosing which classes to cover. Use PartitionDependency instead when the inclusion or exclusion of values in one field is conditional on a value chosen in another field. Use CoverageRequirement instead when you are stating the overall criterion (pairwise, boundary-values, MC/DC) and priority, rather than the per-partition value subset it draws on.

partitionRef.description: ID of the testing.inputspacepartition from which values are being selected for coverage.

coverValues.description: Comma-separated labels or IDs of specific partition values to include in coverage. Ignored when coverAllCategories is true.

coverAllCategories.description: When true, all partition values are included in coverage except those listed in excludeValues. Overrides coverValues.

excludeValues.description: Comma-separated labels or IDs of partition values to exclude from coverage. Applied when coverAllCategories is true to carve out specific values.

inputpartitionselection.x-dr-standard: IEEE 829-2008 Level Test Design Specification (Clause 10), approach refinements: selection of equivalence classes to be exercised
x-dr-evidence: A combinatorial test model file (e.g. a PICT .txt or ACTS model) that lists one parameter with only a subset of its defined value classes.
A test-design YAML/JSON block keyed by an input field or partition name, with include/exclude lists or an 'all: true, except: [...]' form.
A parametrized test (pytest.mark.parametrize, it.each, @EnumSource(mode = EXCLUDE)) iterating over one field's enum or equivalence classes, with specific classes deliberately omitted or excluded.

x-dr-distinguish.testing.inputselection: a single partition value is bound to a concrete test datum for one specific TestCaseSketch, rather than a set of classes being declared in scope for a requirement.
x-dr-distinguish.testing.partitionvalue: you are defining the equivalence class itself (its label, constraint and representative value), not choosing which classes to cover.
x-dr-distinguish.testing.partitiondependency: the inclusion or exclusion of values in one field is conditional on a value chosen in another field.
x-dr-distinguish.testing.coveragerequirement: you are stating the overall criterion (pairwise, boundary-values, MC/DC) and priority, rather than the per-partition value subset it draws on.

inputselection.title: InputSelection
inputselection.description: A single input binding inside one TestCaseSketch that assigns, for one partitioned input field, the chosen equivalence class (a PartitionValue) and the exact datum the test will submit for it. It is owned by exactly one test case, so it records the data that one test actually uses rather than a coverage obligation. Use InputPartitionSelection instead when the element states which partition values a CoverageRequirement obliges tests to exercise (cover/exclude lists), without fixing a concrete datum for any particular test case. Use PartitionValue instead when the element defines an equivalence class itself (label, constraint, category, representative value) independent of any test case that uses it. Use TestCaseSketch instead when the element is the whole test case design (status, implementation format, source) that groups several input bindings. Use TargetInputField instead when the element only associates an input field of the target with its InputSpacePartition, without choosing a value for a specific test.

partitionRef.description: ID of the testing.inputspacepartition whose input field this binding supplies a value for; set it on every selection so the concrete value can be traced to its input dimension.

selectedValue.description: Label or ID of the testing.partitionvalue (equivalence class) chosen from that partition for this test case, e.g. 'boundary-max' or 'null-empty'.

concreteValue.description: The exact datum the test submits for the field, serialized as a string (literal, JSON fragment, or fixture key), e.g. '255', '""', or 'fixtures/user_admin.json'.

valueSource.description: How the concrete value was obtained: manually authored, algorithmically generated, drawn from a data set, or loaded from a test fixture

inputselection.x-dr-standard: IEEE 829-2008 Clause 11 Level Test Case: inputs
x-dr-evidence: A row in a parametrized test table (e.g. pytest.mark.parametrize, JUnit @CsvSource, Jest test.each) that supplies a specific literal for one argument, often named or commented after its class, such as 'age=-1  # invalid: negative'
A test-data file (CSV/JSON/YAML) with one column per input field and one row per test case, consumed by a data-driven runner

A fixture or factory call inside a single test that builds a specific value for a request field, e.g. build_user(email='a@b') or a Faker/hypothesis strategy pinned to a boundary such as max length 255

x-dr-distinguish.testing.inputpartitionselection: the element states which partition values a CoverageRequirement obliges tests to exercise (cover/exclude lists), without fixing a concrete datum for any particular test case
x-dr-distinguish.testing.partitionvalue: the element defines an equivalence class itself (label, constraint, category, representative value) independent of any test case that uses it
x-dr-distinguish.testing.testcasesketch: the element is the whole test case design (status, implementation format, source) that groups several input bindings
x-dr-distinguish.testing.targetinputfield: the element only associates an input field of the target with its InputSpacePartition, without choosing a value for a specific test

inputspacepartition.title: InputSpacePartition
inputspacepartition.description: A test-design artifact that divides the domain of a single input field (an API parameter, schema property, or stored collection attribute) into a named set of equivalence classes (PartitionValues), each grouping values expected to produce the same behaviour under test. It also states whether that field must be present in test inputs. Use PartitionValue instead when the element is one individual equivalence class (label, constraint, representative value) rather than the whole set of classes for a field. Use InputPartitionSelection instead when the element chooses which classes of an existing partition a CoverageRequirement must exercise, rather than defining the classes themselves. Use TargetInputField instead when the element only binds a field of a specific TestCoverageTarget to a partition and records its relevance, without enumerating classes. Use PartitionDependency instead when the element expresses a constraint linking a class in one field's partition to the allowed classes of another field.

description.description: Free-text explanation of the input dimension being partitioned and the basis on which its equivalence classes were derived (e.g. specification rule, data type limits); set whenever the partitioning rationale is not obvious from the field name.

fieldRef.description: Cross-layer ID of the input field this partition divides, typically an api.parameter, data-model.schemaproperty, data-model.jsonschema or data-store.collection element; always set to the single field whose value domain is being partitioned.

presenceRule.description: Whether this input field must be present in test inputs for this partition

inputspacepartition.x-dr-standard: IEEE 829-2008 Level Test Design Specification (test approach refinements / features to be tested); equivalence partitioning technique as defined in ISO/IEC/IEEE 29119-4 §5.2.1
x-dr-evidence: a parametrized test table (e.g. pytest.mark.parametrize, JUnit @ParameterizedTest with @MethodSource, Jest test.each) for one input field whose cases carry class ids such as 'valid', 'empty', 'too_long', 'negative'

a test-data module, enum or factory that enumerates named valid/invalid/boundary value groups for a single request parameter or schema property (e.g. EMAIL_CASES = {valid: [...], malformed: [...], null: [...]})

a property-based generator per field built from named sub-strategies (e.g. hypothesis st.one_of(valid_emails(), malformed_emails())), or a test-design document table listing equivalence classes per parameter

x-dr-distinguish.testing.partitionvalue: the element is one individual equivalence class (label, constraint, representative value) rather than the whole set of classes for a field
x-dr-distinguish.testing.inputpartitionselection: the element chooses which classes of an existing partition a CoverageRequirement must exercise, rather than defining the classes themselves
x-dr-distinguish.testing.targetinputfield: the element only binds a field of a specific TestCoverageTarget to a partition and records its relevance, without enumerating classes
x-dr-distinguish.testing.partitiondependency: the element expresses a constraint linking a class in one field's partition to the allowed classes of another field

outcomecategory.title: OutcomeCategory
outcomecategory.description: A test-design classification of the observable result a TestCoverageTarget can produce (success, validation error, authorization error, not-found, server error, exception, timeout), stated at the level of result class rather than exact expected value. Coverage requirements must exercise it, and test case sketches are grouped under it. Use PartitionValue instead when the category classifies an input value (e.g. an invalid or null-empty equivalence class) rather than the result the target returns. Use ContextVariation instead when the category describes the test type or execution condition (functional, load, security, regression) under which the target is exercised, not what it returns. Use TestCaseSketch instead when the element specifies a particular case with concrete inputs and a specific expected value or assertion, rather than a class of outcomes. Use EnvironmentFactor instead when the element is the environmental condition (e.g. network latency) that provokes an outcome such as a timeout, rather than the outcome itself.

description.description: Free-text explanation of what observable behaviour qualifies as this outcome for the target, e.g. 'HTTP 422 with field-level error list'. Set it whenever the outcomeType alone does not identify the signal tests should check.

outcomeType.description: The class of observable outcome this category represents, used to group test cases by expected result type for coverage analysis and reporting.

outcomecategory.x-dr-standard: IEEE 829-2008 Level Test Design Specification (feature pass/fail criteria) and Level Test Case Specification (outputs specification)
x-dr-evidence: test describe/context blocks or test names grouped by result class, e.g. 'returns 404 when resource missing', 'rejects unauthorized caller with 403', 'times out after 5s'
parameterized test tables or fixtures with an expected-outcome column (expected_status, expected_error, expectedOutcome) whose values are status classes or error types rather than exact payloads

assertions that check outcome class rather than exact value, e.g. expect(res.status).toBe(400), pytest.raises(ValidationError), assertThrows(AccessDeniedException), or OpenAPI response codes enumerated per operation in test plans

x-dr-distinguish.testing.partitionvalue: the category classifies an input value (e.g. an invalid or null-empty equivalence class) rather than the result the target returns
x-dr-distinguish.testing.contextvariation: the category describes the test type or execution condition (functional, load, security, regression) under which the target is exercised, not what it returns
x-dr-distinguish.testing.testcasesketch: the element specifies a particular case with concrete inputs and a specific expected value or assertion, rather than a class of outcomes
x-dr-distinguish.testing.environmentfactor: the element is the environmental condition (e.g. network latency) that provokes an outcome such as a timeout, rather than the outcome itself

partitiondependency.title: PartitionDependency
partitiondependency.description: A cross-field constraint in combinatorial test design stating that when a specific partition value (the trigger) is selected in one InputSpacePartition, the availability of named partition values in another input field is excluded, required, restricted, or re-ranged, so that generated combinations omit invalid inputs. Use PartitionValue instead when the condition bounds a single field's own equivalence class (its constraintExpression) and does not depend on the value chosen for any other field. Use InputPartitionSelection instead when the restriction is a per-CoverageRequirement choice of which values of one partition to cover or exclude (coverValues/excludeValues), not a rule that applies whenever another field takes a given value. Use InputSpacePartition instead when you are describing the input dimension itself and its presenceRule (including a plain 'conditional' flag), rather than the specific trigger value and affected values that make it conditional. Use CoverageExclusion instead when a target or requirement is deliberately removed from coverage with an approver and accepted risk, rather than a combination being logically invalid.

dependsOnPartition.description: ID of the testing.inputspacepartition that triggers this dependency

dependsOnValue.description: Label or ID of the testing.partitionvalue that activates this dependency

effect.description: How the dependency affects the related partition values

affectedValues.description: Comma-separated labels or IDs of the partition values in the dependent field whose availability is modified by this dependency (e.g., values that are excluded, required, or restricted when the trigger value is selected).

description.description: Free-text explanation of the business or technical reason the trigger value constrains the affected values (e.g. 'guest accounts cannot hold admin role'); set whenever the rule is not self-evident from effect and affectedValues.

partitiondependency.x-dr-standard: IEEE 829-2008 Level Test Design Specification (test design refinements: feature/input combinations to be tested); conceptually the category-partition method's selector constraints (Ostrand & Balcer)
x-dr-evidence: A constraint line in a combinatorial test model file, e.g. a PICT/ACTS model containing 'IF [PaymentMethod] = "invoice" THEN [Country] IN {"DE","AT"};'

A parametrized test generator (e.g. pytest_generate_tests, JUnit ArgumentsProvider, itertools.product filter) that drops or skips tuples when one parameter has a specific value and another has a listed value
A property-based test calling assume()/filter() that ties one generated argument's allowed values to another argument's value, e.g. 'assume(not (account_type == "guest" and role == "admin"))'

x-dr-distinguish.testing.inputpartitionselection: the restriction is a per-CoverageRequirement choice of which values of one partition to cover or exclude (coverValues/excludeValues), not a rule that applies whenever another field takes a given value.

partitionvalue.title: PartitionValue
partitionvalue.description: A single equivalence class or boundary class of one input dimension, owned by exactly one InputSpacePartition. It is defined by a boundary condition and by a representative value that stands for every value in the class during test design. Use InputSpacePartition instead when you are modelling the whole input field or dimension and its complete set of classes, rather than one class within it. Use InputSelection instead when you are binding a specific concrete test datum, used by a particular TestCaseSketch, to one of the partition's classes. Use InputPartitionSelection instead when you are stating which classes of a partition a CoverageRequirement must or must not exercise. Use OutcomeCategory instead when the category classifies expected results (success, validation error, timeout) rather than input values.

label.description: Short identifier for the class, unique within its parent partition (e.g. 'empty-string', 'above-max'); other nodes cite it in coverValues, excludeValues and affectedValues, so it is always set.

description.description: Optional free-text explanation of why values in this class are expected to behave alike and what behaviour they probe; set it when the label and constraint alone do not make the intent clear.

constraint.description: Human-readable description of the condition this partition boundary represents (e.g., 'must be between 0 and 100', 'must not be null or empty').

constraintExpression.description: Machine-evaluable expression encoding the partition boundary condition (e.g., a regex pattern, JSONPath predicate, or comparison expression such as 'value >= 0 && value <= 100').

category.description: Equivalence partition category for this value

representativeValue.description: One abstract value, written as a string, that stands for the whole class in test design (e.g. '101' for above-max, '' for null-empty); it is distinct from the concrete datum later bound in InputSelection.concreteValue.

targetcoveragesummary.title: TargetCoverageSummary
targetcoveragesummary.description: A per-target coverage report record that states, for exactly one TestCoverageTarget, the counts of designed, implemented and automated test case sketches and the share of that target's coverage requirements exercised by at least one implemented test. It reports measured status, not required criteria or identified deficits. Use CoverageSummary instead when the record aggregates totals across all targets and requirements of a whole TestCoverageModel rather than metrics for one target. Use CoverageGap instead when the element records a specific uncovered requirement with severity and remediation status, rather than numeric coverage counts. Use CoverageRequirement instead when the element specifies the coverage criteria a target must satisfy, rather than reporting how far they are satisfied. Use TestCoverageTarget instead when the element identifies the endpoint, workflow or component in scope for testing, rather than its coverage metrics.

targetRef.description: ID of the testing.testcoveragetarget this summary covers

sketchCount.description: Total number of TestCaseSketch nodes for this target (design-time count; superset of implementedCount)

implementedCount.description: Number of sketches with a concrete test case implementation (must be ≤ sketchCount; superset of automatedCount)

automatedCount.description: Number of implemented test cases that are automated (must be ≤ implementedCount)

coveragePercentage.description: Percentage of coverage requirements with at least one implemented test case sketch (0–100)

targetinputfield.title: TargetInputField
targetinputfield.description: A test-design association that binds one input field of a TestCoverageTarget's artifact (an API parameter, data-model property or UI input) to the InputSpacePartition used to divide that field into equivalence classes. It also records whether the field must appear in test inputs for that target. Use InputSpacePartition instead when you are defining the equivalence classes of an input dimension itself, independent of which target or field uses them. Use InputPartitionSelection instead when you are stating which values of a partition a specific CoverageRequirement must exercise, rather than which partition governs a target's field. Use InputSelection instead when you are binding a concrete test datum to a partition value for an individual TestCaseSketch. Use TestCoverageTarget instead when the symbol represents the endpoint, workflow or component under test as a whole, not one of its input fields.

testcasesketch.title: TestCaseSketch
testcasesketch.description: A single test case design that combines specific input selections (one chosen value per relevant partition), a context variation and an expected outcome category to exercise one CoverageRequirement of a TestCoverageTarget. It may remain unimplemented or be linked through source to the individual test function, parameterized row or scenario that realizes it. Use CoverageRequirement instead when the element states which partitions, contexts or outcomes must be covered (the criterion), rather than one specific combination chosen to satisfy it. Use InputSelection instead when the element is one field's binding of a partition representative to a concrete datum inside a test case, not the whole test case. Use InputPartitionSelection instead when the element lists which partition values a coverage requirement demands across all its tests, rather than the values one test case uses. Use TestCoverageTarget instead when the element identifies the endpoint, component or workflow under test, which anchors many test cases, rather than an individual test case against it.

description.description: Free-text summary of the scenario this sketch exercises: preconditions, the input combination chosen and the expected observable outcome. Set it whenever the name alone does not make the intent clear.

status.description: Lifecycle status of the test case sketch

testcoveragemodel.title: TestCoverageModel
testcoveragemodel.description: A versioned, application-scoped coverage specification that acts as the root container for the coverage targets, input partitions, context variations, coverage requirements, exclusions and test case sketches of exactly one application or API. It corresponds to a test plan as a whole, not to any individual target, test, suite or results report. Use TestCoverageTarget instead when the element identifies one endpoint, workflow, UI component, job or integration flow that needs coverage, rather than the whole application's coverage specification. Use CoverageSummary instead when the element reports aggregated counts or status across a model's targets, requirements and sketches, rather than defining the coverage scope itself. Use CoverageRequirement instead when the element states the criteria (partitions, contexts, outcomes, coverage strategy) that a single target must satisfy, rather than containing all targets and requirements.

version.description: Version identifier of this coverage model, as a semantic version or date stamp (e.g. '1.2.0' or '2024-05-01'); increment it whenever targets, requirements or exclusions are added, removed or changed.

application.description: Cross-layer reference ID to the application or API element (application layer or api layer) being covered by this model

description.description: Free-text summary of the model's scope, the application release or test level it addresses, and any overall test approach; set it whenever the scope is not obvious from the application reference.

source.description: Provenance information indicating the origin of this model (e.g., manually authored, imported from OpenAPI, or generated from source artifacts)

testcoveragetarget.title: TestCoverageTarget
testcoveragetarget.description: A test-scope entry in a TestCoverageModel that names one production artifact or capability (an API operation, UI view, business workflow, data migration, integration flow or scheduled job) whose behaviour must be verified. It is the anchor to which input fields, outcome categories, coverage requirements and test case sketches for that artifact attach. It records what is in scope, not the production code itself. Use CoverageRequirement instead when the element states the criteria (e.g. boundary-values, pairwise) that must be exercised for a target, rather than naming the thing to be tested. Use TestCaseSketch instead when the element is an individual designed or implemented test case selecting specific partition values, rather than the artifact those cases exercise. Use TestCoverageModel instead when the element is the application-wide root aggregating many targets, partitions and requirements, rather than a single artifact in scope. Use TargetCoverageSummary instead when the element reports sketch, implemented or automated counts and a percentage for a target, rather than defining the target.

description.description: Free-text summary of the artifact or functionality in scope and the testing concerns it raises. Set it whenever the target name and targetType alone do not make the boundary of what must be verified clear.

targetType.description: The kind of artifact or functionality requiring test coverage

priority.description: Relative importance of achieving coverage for this target

source.description: Source code reference for the artifact requiring test coverage
